name: Dark Chocolate Date Truffles
steps: Blitz almonds in a food processor until finely chopped.
Add dates, cocoa powder and vanilla. Blend until a sticky dough forms.
Roll into 12 balls. Freeze for 10 minutes.
Dip in melted chocolate, sprinkle sea salt. Refrigerate until set.
benefits: Natural sugars from dates provide sustained energy
85% dark chocolate delivers antioxidant flavanols
No refined sugar or artificial ingredients
tip: Roll uncoated balls in cocoa powder or crushed pistachios for a quick variation.

name: Cashew Vanilla Cheesecake Bites
steps: Base: blend dates and coconut until sticky. Press into a lined mini-muffin tray.
Filling: blend drained cashews, coconut cream, lemon, honey and vanilla until silky smooth.
Spoon filling over bases. Freeze for 3 hours until set.
Pop out and serve chilled.
benefits: Cashews provide heart-healthy monounsaturated fats
Lemon juice brightens flavour without extra sugar
Dairy-free and refined-sugar-free
tip: Top with a berry or a drizzle of raw honey just before serving.

name: Coconut Cacao Bark
steps: Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Spread melted chocolate evenly about 3mm thick.
Scatter coconut, cacao nibs, almonds and sea salt over the top.
Refrigerate for 30 minutes until fully set. Break into shards.
benefits: Cacao nibs are among the richest sources of magnesium
Dark chocolate antioxidants support cardiovascular health
No added sugar beyond chocolate's natural content
tip: Add dried raspberries or orange zest to the melted chocolate for a gourmet twist.

name: Raw Honey Almond Brittle
steps: Mix honey and coconut oil in a bowl. Add almonds and coat thoroughly.
Spread on a lined baking sheet, sprinkle cinnamon and salt.
Refrigerate or freeze for 20 minutes until hardened.
Break into pieces and store in an airtight container.
benefits: Almonds are rich in vitamin E and heart-healthy fats
Raw honey retains natural enzymes and antioxidants
High in magnesium for muscle relaxation
tip: Use activated almonds (soaked and dehydrated) for easier digestion.

name: Walnut Cacao Truffles
steps: Pulse walnuts in food processor until finely ground.
Add dates, cacao, almond butter and vanilla. Process until a sticky dough forms.
Roll into 14 balls using damp hands. Coat in cocoa powder.
Chill for 30 minutes before serving.
benefits: Walnuts are the richest nut source of omega-3 fatty acids
Cacao powder is high in iron and magnesium
Dates provide chromium to help regulate blood sugar
tip: Keep refrigerated for up to 2 weeks or freeze for 3 months.

name: Raw Carrot Cake Bites
steps: Pulse walnuts and dates until coarsely combined.
Add grated carrot, coconut and spices. Pulse until mixture sticks together.
Roll into 16 balls. Refrigerate for 20 minutes.
Optional: roll in extra coconut or ground walnuts.
benefits: Carrots provide beta-carotene for skin and eye health
Warming spices have anti-inflammatory properties
Naturally sweetened with only whole fruit
tip: Add a squeeze of orange juice to the mix for a citrus-carrot cake flavour.

name: Raw Blueberry Cheesecake Cups
steps: Base: blend dates and almonds until sticky crumble. Press into cupcake cases.
Filling: blend cashews, coconut oil, lemon and honey until silky.
Blend blueberries separately into a purée.
Swirl cashew cream and blueberry purée into cases. Freeze 2h.
benefits: Blueberries are among the highest antioxidant foods
Cashews provide B vitamins and healthy fats
Refined-sugar-free and dairy-free
tip: Press the base mixture firmly to prevent crumbling when unmoulding.

name: Salted Caramel Pecan Bars
steps: Blend dates, tahini, coconut oil and vanilla to a smooth caramel paste.
Press almond flour and half the pecans into a lined 20cm tin for the base.
Spread date caramel over base.
Press remaining pecans on top. Sprinkle sea salt. Freeze 1h before slicing.
benefits: Pecans are high in zinc, manganese and gamma-tocopherol vitamin E
Tahini adds calcium and sesamin for anti-inflammatory support
Salt enhances natural caramel flavour without sugar
tip: Cut with a warm knife for clean bar edges.

name: Cacao Orange Truffles
steps: Blend dates, cacao, almond flour, orange zest and coconut oil until a dough forms.
Roll into 14 balls. Freeze 15 minutes.
Dip each ball in melted dark chocolate. Let set on parchment.
benefits: Orange zest contains d-limonene, a potent detox compound
Cacao and citrus complement each other's antioxidant profiles
Classic flavour combination in a healthy format
tip: Add a tiny pinch of cayenne for a Mexican chocolate variation.

name: Coconut Lime Bites
steps: Mix all ingredients together in a bowl until a thick dough forms.
Refrigerate 20 minutes to firm up.
Roll into 12 balls. Coat in extra desiccated coconut.
Keep refrigerated up to 1 week.
benefits: Lime provides vitamin C and citric acid for detox support
Coconut MCTs are rapidly used as energy
Bright, refreshing flavour profile
tip: Use toasted coconut on the outside for extra flavour depth.

name: Strawberry Coconut Bars
steps: Pulse coconut with cashews, half the honey and coconut oil until crumbly. Press into a lined tin.
Blend strawberries with remaining honey and vanilla until smooth.
Pour over base. Freeze 2h until set.
Slice into bars and serve chilled.
benefits: Strawberries are rich in vitamin C and ellagic acid
Cashews provide magnesium and healthy fats
Vibrant pink colour from natural fruit
tip: Top with a few fresh strawberry slices for a beautiful finish.

name: Hazelnut Praline Cups
steps: Blend toasted hazelnuts until they form a coarse butter.
Add dates and cacao. Blend to a paste.
Press into silicone cupcake mould cups.
Melt chocolate with coconut cream. Pour over hazelnut base. Sprinkle salt.
Freeze 1.5h. Unmould and serve.
benefits: Hazelnuts are exceptionally high in vitamin E for skin health
Naturally resembles a healthier Ferrero Rocher
Toasting amplifies hazelnut flavour without extra ingredients
tip: Toast hazelnuts at 180°C for 8-10 minutes until skins crack — rub off skins with a towel for a cleaner flavour.

name: 3-Ingredient Banana Nice Cream
steps: Peel and freeze bananas overnight until solid.
Blend frozen banana pieces until smooth and creamy — scrape sides as needed.
Add peanut butter and vanilla, blend briefly.
Serve immediately as soft-serve or freeze for 1h for firmer consistency.
benefits: Ripe bananas are high in potassium and natural prebiotics
Contains no dairy, refined sugar or artificial additives
Quick source of natural energy post-workout
tip: Blend in frozen mango or strawberries for different flavours. Top with cacao nibs for crunch.

name: Mango Coconut Popsicles
steps: Blend mango, coconut milk, lime juice and honey until completely smooth.
Pour into popsicle moulds, top with coconut flakes.
Insert sticks and freeze for at least 4 hours.
Run warm water over moulds briefly to release.
benefits: Mango is exceptionally high in vitamin C and folate
Coconut milk provides medium-chain triglycerides for quick energy
Dairy-free and perfect for hot days
tip: Layer mango and coconut layers by alternating two blended mixtures for a beautiful two-tone effect.

name: Berry Frozen Yogurt Bark
steps: Mix yogurt, honey and vanilla until smooth.
Spread evenly 1cm thick on a lined baking sheet.
Scatter berries and granola over the top, pressing gently.
Freeze for 3-4 hours until solid. Break into shards and serve immediately.
benefits: Greek yogurt provides 6g protein per serving plus gut-friendly probiotics
Berries are among the highest antioxidant foods available
Low calorie and nutrient-dense
tip: Make this on a Sunday for a week's worth of healthy dessert — stored in a freezer bag.

name: Watermelon Mint Granita
steps: Blend watermelon, lime, mint and honey until smooth.
Pour into a wide, flat freezer-safe dish.
Freeze for 1 hour, then scrape with a fork every 30 minutes for 3 hours.
Serve fluffed into glasses or bowls.
benefits: Watermelon is 92% water for excellent hydration
Contains lycopene, a powerful antioxidant linked to heart health
Only 55 kcal per serving — ideal for weight management
tip: Add a splash of coconut water instead of plain water for extra electrolytes.

name: Chocolate Coconut Fudge Pops
steps: Warm coconut milk in a saucepan over low heat.
Add chocolate and stir until melted. Remove from heat.
Whisk in cacao powder, maple syrup and vanilla.
Cool slightly, pour into moulds and freeze overnight.
benefits: Coconut milk MCTs support steady energy
Antioxidant-rich dark chocolate
Dairy-free alternative to ice cream
tip: Stir in a tablespoon of almond butter for extra creaminess and protein.

name: Frozen Acai Sorbet
steps: Break frozen acai into chunks.
Blend acai, banana and berries until thick and smooth (like sorbet).
Sweeten with honey to taste.
Serve immediately in chilled bowls with toppings of choice.
benefits: Acai is one of the highest antioxidant foods in the world
Rich in anthocyanins linked to improved brain health
High fiber supports digestive wellness
tip: Top with granola, banana slices and a drizzle of honey for an acai bowl experience.

name: Peach Cream Popsicles
steps: Blend peaches, honey and lemon until smooth.
Whisk yogurt with vanilla separately.
Layer fruit purée and yogurt alternately in moulds.
Insert sticks, freeze 4+ hours.
benefits: Peaches are rich in beta-carotene and vitamin C
Greek yogurt adds protein and probiotics
Under 85 kcal per popsicle
tip: Ripe, fragrant peaches make all the difference — use them at peak season.

name: Kiwi Lime Sorbet
steps: Blend all ingredients until completely smooth.
Freeze in a shallow dish for 1h, then scrape.
Repeat scraping every 30 minutes for 2-3 hours.
Serve in chilled bowls with a sprig of mint.
benefits: Kiwi has more vitamin C per gram than oranges
High in vitamin K for bone health
Naturally low calorie and hydrating
tip: Gold kiwi makes a beautifully sweet, less tart version of this sorbet.

name: Blueberry Banana Nice Cream
steps: Blend frozen bananas and blueberries until beginning to come together.
Add almond milk and vanilla, blend until smooth and thick.
Serve immediately as soft-serve or freeze 45 minutes for scoopable texture.
Top with fresh berries or granola.
benefits: Blueberries provide anthocyanins for brain and heart health
Bananas add potassium and natural sweetness
Zero refined sugar, dairy-free, whole-food dessert
tip: The ratio of frozen banana to blueberry controls sweetness — adjust to taste.

name: Cherry Chocolate Freezer Bars
steps: Blend cherries, coconut milk, cacao, maple syrup and vanilla until smooth.
Pour into a lined 20x10cm loaf tin or bar moulds.
Freeze at least 4h until solid.
Slice and serve immediately, or store in individual pieces in a zip-lock bag.
benefits: Cherries are rich in melatonin supporting natural sleep cycles
Anthocyanins in cherries reduce post-exercise muscle soreness
Chocolate-cherry combination is rich in polyphenols
tip: Use sour cherries for a more intense, less sweet flavour that pairs beautifully with dark chocolate.

name: Strawberry Lemonade Popsicles
steps: Blend all ingredients until smooth.
Taste and adjust sweetness with honey.
Pour into popsicle moulds.
Freeze at least 5 hours or overnight.
benefits: Strawberries are very high in vitamin C and antioxidants
Only 48 kcal per popsicle
Refreshing and hydrating on hot days
tip: Add a splash of rose water for an elegant twist.

name: Matcha Coconut Ice Cream
steps: Whisk matcha into 2 tbsp warm coconut milk until smooth paste.
Blend with remaining coconut milk, honey, vanilla and salt.
Refrigerate mixture 2h, then churn in ice cream maker, OR freeze 3h stirring every 45 minutes.
Serve in chilled bowls.
benefits: Matcha provides sustained energy and L-theanine for calm focus
Dairy-free and vegan
Green tea catechins support metabolism
tip: Refrigerating the mixture before freezing gives a smoother texture.

name: Almond Flour Banana Muffins
steps: Preheat oven to 180°C / 350°F. Line a 12-cup muffin tray.
Whisk eggs, mashed banana, honey and vanilla.
Stir in almond flour, baking soda and cinnamon until combined.
Fold in chocolate chips. Divide into muffin cups.
Bake 20-22 minutes until a skewer comes out clean.
benefits: Almond flour provides more protein and less carbs than wheat flour
Naturally sweetened by ripe bananas and a touch of honey
Gluten-free and grain-free
tip: Freeze baked muffins for up to 2 months. Reheat for 30 seconds from frozen.

name: Honey Oat Flapjacks
steps: Preheat oven to 175°C / 345°F. Line a square 20cm tin.
Melt coconut oil and honey together over low heat.
Add oats, seeds, cranberries and cinnamon. Mix well.
Press firmly into tin. Bake 18-20 minutes until golden.
Cool completely before cutting into 12 bars.
benefits: Oats provide beta-glucan fibre to lower cholesterol
Seeds add zinc, magnesium and omega-3 fatty acids
Sustained energy release — ideal pre or post workout
tip: Press mixture very firmly into the tin before baking for bars that hold together cleanly.

name: Coconut Macaroons
steps: Preheat oven to 165°C / 330°F. Line a baking sheet.
Lightly whisk egg whites with honey, vanilla and almond extract.
Fold in desiccated coconut until evenly coated.
Heap tablespoons onto sheet. Bake 15-18 minutes until golden.
Cool fully. Dip bases in melted chocolate if desired.
benefits: Coconut provides medium-chain triglycerides for energy
Lower in carbs than traditional biscuits
Naturally gluten-free and dairy-free
tip: Slightly underbake for a chewy centre — they firm up further as they cool.

name: Peanut Butter Oat Cookies
steps: Preheat oven to 180°C / 350°F.
Mix peanut butter, mashed banana and honey until combined.
Stir in oats, chocolate chips and salt.
Scoop onto baking sheet. Flatten slightly. Bake 12-14 minutes.
Cool on tray — they firm up as they cool.
benefits: Peanut butter provides protein and niacin for metabolism support
Banana naturally sweetens without added sugar
3-ingredient base — infinitely adaptable
tip: Add a sprinkle of flaked sea salt on top before baking for a salted caramel flavour.

name: Tahini Date Brownies
steps: Preheat oven to 175°C / 350°F. Line a 20cm square tin.
Blend dates until smooth paste forms.
Whisk in tahini, eggs and vanilla.
Fold in cacao, baking powder and salt until combined.
Bake 18-22 minutes — centre should be slightly fudgy.
Cool completely before cutting.
benefits: Tahini provides calcium and sesame lignans with anti-inflammatory effects
Dates replace refined sugar with fibre and minerals
Gluten-free and grain-free
tip: Top with a sesame-seed cacao glaze for a Middle-Eastern inspired finish.

name: Black Bean Brownies
steps: Preheat oven to 175°C / 350°F. Grease a 20cm square tin.
Blend black beans until smooth.
Add eggs, cacao, honey, oil and vanilla — blend until silky.
Stir in baking powder and chocolate chips.
Pour into tin. Bake 22-25 minutes.
Cool fully before slicing.
benefits: Black beans add 6g protein and 3.5g fibre per brownie
No flour needed — gluten-free and high satiety
Beans provide resistant starch for gut microbiome health
tip: Nobody will guess there are beans inside — the flavour is pure chocolate.

name: Peach Almond Crumble
steps: Preheat oven to 190°C / 375°F.
Toss peaches with half the honey and cinnamon. Place in baking dish.
Rub almond flour, oats, coconut oil and remaining honey into crumble texture.
Stir in flaked almonds. Scatter evenly over peaches.
Bake 25-30 minutes until bubbling and golden.
benefits: Peaches are rich in vitamin C, A and potassium
Almond flour crumble adds protein and vitamin E
Naturally gluten-free with wholesome ingredients
tip: Serve warm with a dollop of coconut yogurt or a small scoop of banana nice cream.

name: Cinnamon Baked Apples
steps: Preheat oven to 180°C / 350°F.
Core apples leaving base intact. Place in baking dish with ½ cup water.
Mix oats, walnuts, honey, oil, cinnamon and raisins.
Fill apple cavities with oat mixture.
Bake 25-30 minutes until apples are tender. Serve warm.
benefits: Apples provide pectin fibre that feeds beneficial gut bacteria
Cinnamon helps regulate blood sugar spikes after eating
High fibre makes this surprisingly filling
tip: Use Braeburn or Cox apples for the best texture — they hold their shape when baked.

name: Sweet Potato Brownies
steps: Preheat oven to 180°C / 350°F. Line a 20cm tin.
Whisk sweet potato, almond butter, honey and eggs until smooth.
Stir in cacao, baking powder and vanilla.
Pour into tin. Bake 22-25 minutes — centre should be just set.
Cool completely before slicing.
benefits: Sweet potato adds beta-carotene and fibre invisibly
Gluten-free, grain-free and nutrient-dense
Almond butter provides protein and vitamin E
tip: The fudgier these are when they come out of the oven the better — they firm up as they cool.

name: Zucchini Chocolate Cake
steps: Preheat oven to 175°C / 350°F. Grease a 20cm round tin.
Squeeze excess water from grated zucchini.
Whisk eggs, maple syrup and coconut oil together.
Fold in almond flour, cacao and baking soda.
Stir in zucchini.
Bake 28-32 minutes. Cool before slicing.
benefits: Zucchini adds moisture and nutrients invisibly
Higher protein and lower glycaemic than conventional cake
Gluten-free and grain-free
tip: Frost with a thin layer of dark chocolate ganache for an impressive presentation.

name: Lemon Poppy Seed Muffins
steps: Preheat oven to 175°C / 350°F. Line a 12-hole muffin tin.
Whisk eggs, honey, coconut oil, lemon zest and juice.
Fold in almond flour, baking soda and poppy seeds.
Divide between cases. Bake 18-20 minutes until golden.
Cool before serving.
benefits: Bright citrus flavour without artificial extracts
Almond flour makes these grain-free and protein-rich
Poppy seeds are a good source of calcium and manganese
tip: Drizzle with a thin lemon-honey glaze while still warm for extra moisture.

name: Carrot Walnut Loaf
steps: Preheat oven to 175°C / 350°F. Line a loaf tin.
Whisk eggs, maple syrup and coconut oil.
Fold in almond flour, cinnamon and baking powder.
Stir in carrots and walnuts.
Bake 40-45 minutes until a skewer is clean. Cool before slicing.
benefits: Walnuts provide omega-3 fats and melatonin precursors
Carrots add beta-carotene and natural sweetness
Gluten-free and grain-free
tip: Keeps well refrigerated for 4 days, or freeze individual slices.

name: Buckwheat Honey Cake
steps: Preheat oven to 175°C / 350°F. Grease a 20cm round tin.
Whisk eggs, honey, coconut oil and almond milk.
Fold in buckwheat flour, cinnamon and baking powder.
Bake 28-32 minutes until set. Cool before serving.
benefits: Buckwheat is naturally gluten-free and high in rutin for blood vessel health
Lower glycaemic index than wheat flour
Nutty flavour pairs beautifully with honey
tip: Dust with buckwheat flour and serve with fresh fruit for an elegant presentation.

name: Oat Berry Crumble Bars
steps: Preheat oven to 180°C / 350°F. Line a 20x30cm tin.
Mix oats, almond flour, coconut oil, honey and cinnamon.
Press ⅔ of oat mixture into the tin.
Toss berries with chia seeds and spread over base.
Crumble remaining oat mixture on top.
Bake 28-32 minutes until golden. Cool before cutting.
benefits: Beta-glucan from oats lowers LDL cholesterol
Berries add concentrated antioxidants and vitamin C
Chia seeds help the berry layer set naturally
tip: Refrigerate before cutting for clean bar edges.

name: Avocado Chocolate Mousse
steps: Halve, stone and scoop avocados into a blender.
Add all remaining ingredients.
Blend until completely smooth and glossy — 2-3 minutes.
Taste and adjust sweetness.
Chill for 30 minutes. Serve in glasses with berries on top.
benefits: Avocado provides glutathione, the body's master antioxidant
Monounsaturated fats support hormone production
Creamy without any dairy — vegan-friendly
tip: The mousse keeps for 24h in the fridge with plastic wrap pressed against the surface.

name: Chia Seed Mango Pudding
steps: Mix chia seeds, coconut milk and honey. Stir well.
Refrigerate for at least 2 hours (or overnight), stirring once after 30 minutes.
Blend mango with lime zest into a smooth purée.
Layer chia pudding and mango purée in glasses.
Top with extra mango cubes and mint.
benefits: Chia seeds provide 8g fibre per serving — exceptional for gut health
Complete omega-3 source from plant-based seeds
Mango delivers vitamin C, A and folate
tip: Prepare the night before for a perfect grab-and-go breakfast-style dessert.

name: Coconut Vanilla Panna Cotta
steps: Dissolve gelatin in 3 tbsp cold water; leave 5 minutes.
Warm coconut milk with honey and vanilla over medium heat until steaming — do not boil.
Whisk in dissolved gelatin until fully combined.
Pour into 4 moulds or glasses. Refrigerate 4 hours until set.
Serve with berry coulis drizzled over.
benefits: Coconut milk is naturally dairy-free with a rich creamy texture
MCTs in coconut milk support cognitive function
Elegant, restaurant-quality dessert with 5 ingredients
tip: Use agar-agar instead of gelatin for a fully vegan version — adjust quantity per packet instructions.

name: Raspberry Chia Fool
steps: Mash half the raspberries with honey to make a rough coulis.
Stir chia seeds into Greek yogurt with vanilla. Rest 15 minutes to thicken.
Layer yogurt mixture and raspberry coulis in glasses.
Top with whole raspberries and a drizzle of honey.
benefits: Raspberries contain more fibre than almost any other fruit
Greek yogurt contributes 7g protein and live probiotic cultures
Under 120 kcal per serving
tip: Swap raspberries for strawberries or mixed summer berries depending on season.

name: Golden Milk Rice Pudding
steps: Combine rice, coconut milk and almond milk in a saucepan.
Cook over low-medium heat, stirring often, for 30 minutes until rice is tender.
Stir in honey, turmeric, cinnamon, cardamom and black pepper.
Serve warm in bowls, drizzled with extra honey and a sprinkle of cinnamon.
benefits: Turmeric curcumin is a potent anti-inflammatory compound
Black pepper increases curcumin absorption by 2000%
Warming and grounding — particularly beneficial in colder months
tip: Make a large batch and reheat individual portions with a splash of almond milk during the week.

name: Dark Chocolate Orange Mousse
steps: Scoop only the solid coconut cream from a chilled tin (discard liquid).
Whip coconut cream until fluffy with an electric mixer.
Melt chocolate and cool slightly. Fold into cream with honey, orange zest and vanilla.
Spoon into glasses. Chill 1h before serving.
benefits: 85% dark chocolate is rich in magnesium and flavanols
Orange zest adds vitamin C and natural aroma without sugar
Dairy-free and silky smooth
tip: The secret is well-chilled coconut cream — chill the tin overnight for best results.

name: Strawberry Banana Pudding
steps: Blend bananas, strawberries and coconut milk until smooth.
Stir in chia seeds and vanilla.
Refrigerate at least 2h or overnight until thick and pudding-like.
Serve topped with sliced strawberries.
benefits: Chia seeds provide omega-3s and 6g fibre per serving
Naturally sweet — zero refined sugar
High in vitamin C from strawberries
tip: Use slightly over-ripe bananas for maximum sweetness and creaminess.

name: Vanilla Almond Custard
steps: Whisk egg yolks, honey and cornstarch together.
Warm almond milk until just steaming. Gradually pour over egg mixture, whisking.
Return to saucepan over medium heat, stirring constantly until thickened.
Stir in vanilla and almond extract. Pour into bowls.
Serve warm or chilled.
benefits: Dairy-free yet rich and creamy
Egg yolks provide choline for brain health
Comforting and lower calorie than traditional custard
tip: Press cling film onto the surface immediately to prevent a skin forming as it cools.

name: Matcha Coconut Energy Balls
steps: Blend cashews until finely ground.
Add dates, coconut, matcha and honey. Blend until sticky dough forms.
Roll into 12 balls using damp hands.
Roll in coconut flakes. Refrigerate 20 minutes before serving.
benefits: Matcha provides sustained energy via L-theanine without jitteriness
L-theanine promotes calm focus alongside natural caffeine
Antioxidant-rich green tea in a portable format
tip: Use ceremonial grade matcha for a more vibrant colour and smoother flavour.

name: Lemon Chia Energy Bites
steps: Combine all ingredients except coating coconut in a large bowl.
Mix thoroughly until it all sticks together.
Refrigerate mixture for 20 minutes to firm up.
Roll into 14 balls. Coat in desiccated coconut.
Store in fridge for up to 1 week.
benefits: Lemon zest contains d-limonene, a powerful detoxifying compound
Chia seeds expand in the gut for prolonged satiety
High magnesium from oats and almond butter
tip: Refrigerating the mixture before rolling prevents sticky hands and gives a neater ball.

name: Pistachio Rose Bites
steps: Pulse pistachios in a food processor until finely ground, some texture remaining.
Add dates, rose water, cardamom and honey. Blend until sticky.
Roll into 12 balls. Coat in crushed pistachio crumbs.
Refrigerate at least 30 minutes before serving.
benefits: Pistachios are one of the highest protein nuts
Rose water has been used in Persian medicine for mood and digestion
Rich in lutein and zeaxanthin for eye health
tip: These are inspired by Persian sweets — beautiful on a dessert board for entertaining.

name: Turmeric Cashew Bliss Balls
steps: Blend cashews until finely ground.
Add dates, turmeric, black pepper, coconut oil and honey. Blend until dough forms.
Refrigerate for 15 minutes.
Roll into 12 balls. Coat in coconut flakes.
Keep refrigerated for up to 10 days.
benefits: Turmeric curcumin has powerful anti-inflammatory effects
Black pepper dramatically increases curcumin bioavailability
Cashews provide copper and magnesium
tip: These are particularly good during winter months or recovery periods for their anti-inflammatory properties.

name: Espresso Almond Bites
steps: Pulse almonds until finely chopped.
Add dates, espresso, cacao, almond butter and salt. Process until sticky dough forms.
Roll into 12 balls.
Refrigerate at least 20 minutes before serving.
benefits: Natural pre-workout energy from dates and espresso
Almonds provide sustained energy and vitamin E
Rich mocha flavour without any processed ingredients
tip: Use decaf espresso powder for an evening treat without caffeine.

name: Cinnamon Raisin Balls
steps: Mix all ingredients in a bowl until thoroughly combined.
Refrigerate 15 minutes to firm.
Roll into 12 balls.
Store in an airtight container in the fridge up to 1 week.
benefits: Classic spiced flavour reminiscent of an oatmeal cookie
Raisins provide natural iron and quick-release energy
Great mid-morning or pre-workout snack
tip: Soak raisins in warm water for 10 minutes before using for a plumper, juicier result.

name: Hemp Seed Protein Balls
steps: Combine hemp seeds, oats, almond butter, honey and vanilla.
Mix until sticky dough forms. Chill 15 minutes.
Roll into 12 balls. Coat in extra hemp seeds.
Refrigerate up to 1 week.
benefits: Hemp seeds are a complete protein containing all essential amino acids
Rich in omega-3 and omega-6 in an ideal 3:1 ratio
One of the best plant-based protein snacks available
tip: Add a tablespoon of spirulina for an extra plant-protein and micronutrient boost.

name: Chocolate Peanut Butter Bites
steps: Mix peanut butter, honey and vanilla together.
Stir in oats, cacao and chocolate chips.
Chill mixture 20 minutes.
Roll into 14 balls. Keep refrigerated.
benefits: Peanut butter provides niacin, folate and protein
Classic Reese's flavour in a wholefood format
High in magnesium from cacao
tip: Freeze for 30 minutes for a firmer, fudge-like texture.

name: Apricot Sunflower Balls
steps: Pulse sunflower seeds until finely ground.
Add apricots, coconut, honey and cardamom. Process until sticky.
Roll into 14 balls. Coat in extra coconut.
Refrigerate 20 minutes before serving.
benefits: Apricots are high in beta-carotene and natural iron
Sunflower seeds are exceptionally rich in vitamin E
Cardamom supports digestive health
tip: Look for unsulphured apricots — they are brown rather than bright orange and contain no preservatives.

name: Caramelised Banana with Walnut Crumble
steps: Halve bananas lengthways.
Heat coconut oil in a pan over medium-high heat.
Place bananas cut-side down; cook 2-3 minutes until golden.
Drizzle with honey and cinnamon. Flip and cook 1 more minute.
Serve with chopped walnuts and chocolate chips scattered on top.
benefits: Caramelised bananas are high in potassium and vitamin B6
Walnuts add omega-3 fats and create satisfying crunch
Quick, warming dessert ready in under 15 minutes
tip: Serve with coconut yogurt for a complete dessert that still feels indulgent.

name: Honey Roasted Figs with Yogurt
steps: Preheat oven to 200°C / 400°F.
Arrange fig halves cut-side up in a baking dish.
Drizzle with honey and tuck thyme sprigs between them.
Roast for 12-15 minutes until figs are soft and caramelised.
Serve over Greek yogurt topped with walnuts.
benefits: Figs are exceptional in calcium and iron among fresh fruits
Thyme has antimicrobial properties and supports respiratory health
Elegant, seasonal and naturally sweet
tip: Fresh figs are best in late summer. Out of season, use dried figs soaked in warm water.

name: Baked Cinnamon Pears
steps: Preheat oven to 190°C / 375°F.
Halve and core pears. Place cut-side up in a baking dish.
Drizzle with honey, lemon and vanilla. Dust with cinnamon.
Add 4 tbsp water to the dish. Bake 20-25 minutes until tender and golden.
Serve warm with granola and yogurt.
benefits: Pears have one of the highest fibre contents of all common fruits
Only 90 kcal per serving — light and satisfying
Cinnamon helps regulate post-meal blood sugar
tip: Use Conference or Williams pears — they hold their shape during baking beautifully.

name: Grilled Pineapple with Coconut Cream
steps: Heat a grill pan over high heat.
Brush pineapple rings with honey and cinnamon.
Grill 2-3 minutes per side until caramelised and charred.
Whip coconut cream with a pinch of cinnamon.
Serve warm pineapple with coconut cream and fresh mint.
benefits: Pineapple contains bromelain, a potent digestive enzyme and anti-inflammatory
Grilling concentrates natural sugars and intensifies flavour
Only 112 kcal — a light summer dessert
tip: Add a squeeze of lime and a pinch of chilli flakes for a tropical kick.

name: Strawberry Rhubarb Compote
steps: Combine rhubarb, honey and orange juice in a saucepan.
Cook over medium heat 8-10 minutes until rhubarb softens.
Add strawberries and cook 3 more minutes.
Remove from heat, stir in vanilla.
Serve warm over yogurt or nice cream.
benefits: Rhubarb is very high in vitamin K for bone health
Only 72 kcal per serving — very light
High in vitamin C and antioxidants from strawberries
tip: Delicious cold from the fridge the next day — flavours meld and deepen overnight.

name: Citrus Honey Salad
steps: Arrange citrus slices on a serving plate.
Drizzle with honey.
Scatter mint leaves and pomegranate seeds over the top.
Serve immediately or refrigerate up to 2h.
benefits: One of the highest vitamin C servings possible from a dessert
Pomegranate seeds add antioxidant punicalagins
Under 80 kcal — extremely low calorie
tip: Serve alongside a chocolate dessert for a refreshing contrast.

name: Baked Plums with Vanilla
steps: Preheat oven to 200°C / 400°F.
Place plum halves cut-side up in a baking dish.
Drizzle with honey, vanilla and orange zest. Dust with cinnamon.
Bake 15-18 minutes until plums are soft and juicy.
Serve warm with coconut yogurt.
benefits: Plums are high in sorbitol and neochlorogenic acid for digestive health
Very low calorie at just 68 kcal
Baking concentrates natural sweetness
tip: Use Victoria plums or greengages when in season for the best flavour.

name: Tropical Fruit Skewers
steps: Thread fruit alternately onto skewers.
Mix honey, lime juice and chilli flakes (if using) in a small bowl.
Grill or serve raw, drizzled with the honey-lime dressing.
Serve immediately.
benefits: Exceptional vitamin C across four tropical fruits
Bromelain from pineapple aids digestion and reduces inflammation
Naturally low calorie and high in fibre
tip: Grill skewers 2 minutes per side to caramelise natural sugars for a warm dessert option.

name: Poached Pears with Ginger
steps: Combine water, honey, ginger, star anise and cinnamon in a saucepan.
Bring to a simmer. Submerge pears and poach 20-25 minutes until tender.
Remove pears. Reduce poaching liquid by half over high heat.
Serve pears whole with reduced syrup poured over.
benefits: Elegant and naturally sweetened — perfect for entertaining
Ginger soothes digestion and reduces nausea
Pears are exceptionally high in fibre and vitamin K
tip: Add a splash of good quality vanilla extract to the poaching liquid for extra depth.

name: Mango Lime Bowl
steps: Toss diced mango with lime juice, zest and chilli.
Rest 5 minutes to allow flavours to meld.
Serve over coconut yogurt, topped with fresh mint.
benefits: Mango provides over 100% daily vitamin C in one bowl
Lime and chilli activate digestive enzymes
Rich in folate and vitamin A
tip: Use Alphonso or Ataulfo mangoes for the most intense, floral sweetness.

name: Peanut Butter Banana Cups
steps: Line a 10-hole mini muffin tray with paper cases.
Spoon 1 tsp melted chocolate into each case. Freeze 10 minutes.
Mix peanut butter, banana, honey and salt together.
Spoon filling over chocolate bases.
Top with remaining melted chocolate. Freeze 30 minutes.
benefits: Healthy take on a Reese's cup — no refined sugar
Banana provides potassium and prebiotic fibre
Peanut butter adds protein and niacin
tip: Sprinkle flaked sea salt on top before the final chocolate layer sets.

name: Fig and Walnut Energy Squares
steps: Blend walnuts until finely ground.
Add figs, coconut, cinnamon, lemon zest and salt. Blend until sticky dough.
Press firmly into a lined 20cm square tin.
Freeze 30 minutes. Slice into 16 squares.
benefits: Figs are exceptionally high in calcium and iron
Walnuts are rich in omega-3 ALA and brain-protective polyphenols
Lemon zest adds vitamin C and freshness
tip: These keep well at room temperature for 3 days or refrigerated for 2 weeks.

name: Almond Joy Bites
steps: Mix coconut, coconut oil, honey and vanilla until a thick paste forms.
Refrigerate 15 minutes. Form into 12 oval shapes.
Press one almond into each.
Dip each in melted dark chocolate. Refrigerate until set.
benefits: Inspired by Almond Joy — completely refined-sugar-free
Coconut MCTs are rapidly converted to energy
Almonds add vitamin E and healthy monounsaturated fats
tip: Chill the coconut filling thoroughly before dipping in chocolate for neater coating.

name: Banana Oat Pancake Bites
steps: Preheat oven to 180°C / 350°F. Grease a 12-hole muffin tray.
Blend oats into fine flour.
Mix banana, eggs, vanilla and cinnamon. Stir in oat flour and baking powder.
Fold in blueberries. Divide into muffin holes.
Bake 12-15 minutes until set.
benefits: Only 82 kcal per bite — great for calorie-conscious snacking
No refined sugar or flour — gluten-free option
Blueberries add antioxidants and vitamin C
tip: Serve with a drizzle of honey or pure maple syrup for a fun breakfast-dessert crossover.

name: Spiced Pumpkin Cookies
steps: Preheat oven to 175°C / 350°F. Line a baking sheet.
Mix pumpkin, maple syrup and coconut oil.
Stir in oats, almond flour and spices until combined.
Scoop tablespoon-sized mounds onto sheet. Flatten slightly.
Bake 14-16 minutes until firm and golden.
benefits: Pumpkin is packed with beta-carotene, vitamin C and potassium
Warming spice blend supports circulation and digestion
Under 100 kcal per cookie
tip: These cookies taste even better the day after baking as the spices develop.

name: Coconut Lemon Tart
steps: Base: blend almonds, coconut and dates until sticky. Press into a lined tart tin.
Filling: blend cashews, lemon juice, zest, coconut oil and honey until silky smooth.
Pour filling over base. Freeze 2h until set.
Thaw 10 minutes before slicing. Garnish with lemon zest.
benefits: Lemon provides vitamin C and alkalising citric acid
Cashews create a creamy, dairy-free curd texture
Grain-free and refined-sugar-free
tip: Use a loose-bottomed tart tin for easy unmoulding and a professional finish.

name: Banana Split Bowls
steps: Halve bananas lengthways and place in bowls.
Arrange strawberries and pineapple alongside.
Dollop Greek yogurt in the centre.
Drizzle with chocolate sauce and scatter walnuts.
Serve immediately.
benefits: Classic banana split reimagined with only whole foods
Three fruits provide wide spectrum of vitamins and antioxidants
High potassium and fibre
tip: Make the chocolate sauce by warming 1 tbsp dark chocolate with 1 tsp coconut oil.

name: Raspberry Coconut Tarts
steps: Base: process almonds, coconut and dates into sticky crumble. Press into 8 tart moulds.
Blend cashews, raspberries, honey and coconut oil until smooth.
Pour filling over bases. Freeze 2h.
Top with a few fresh raspberries. Thaw 5 minutes before serving.
benefits: Raspberries contain ellagic acid and the highest fibre of common berries
Cashew cream is a versatile dairy-free alternative
Beautiful pink colour entirely from natural fruit
tip: Add a pinch of rose water to the raspberry cream for a romantic floral note.

name: Ginger Snap Bites
steps: Blend almond flour, dates, ginger, cinnamon and coconut oil until dough forms.
Add molasses if using — mix well.
Roll into 14 balls.
Roll each in finely chopped crystallised ginger.
Refrigerate 20 minutes before serving.
benefits: Fresh ginger has powerful anti-nausea and anti-inflammatory properties
Gingerbread flavour profile without refined sugar
Almond flour provides protein and vitamin E
tip: Double the ginger for a bold, warming bite perfect for winter months.

name: Quinoa Chocolate Pudding
steps: Warm coconut milk with cacao and honey, whisking until smooth.
Stir in cooked quinoa and vanilla.
Simmer 5 minutes, stirring, until thickened like rice pudding.
Stir in chocolate chips. Serve warm or chilled.
benefits: Quinoa is a complete protein providing all 9 essential amino acids
Higher in protein than any other grain-based pudding
Chocolate craving satisfied with real cacao antioxidants
tip: Top with a swirl of almond butter and a pinch of flaked sea salt for extra indulgence.

name: Peanut Butter Fudge Bars
steps: Mix peanut butter, coconut oil, honey and vanilla until smooth.
Pour into a lined 20cm square tin. Freeze 20 minutes until firm.
Spread melted chocolate evenly over the top. Sprinkle sea salt.
Freeze 30 more minutes. Slice into 16 bars.
benefits: High protein and satiating — ideal to curb sweet cravings
Chocolate layer adds antioxidant flavanols
Refined-sugar-free, no baking required
tip: The fudge layer needs to be very cold before adding chocolate — or it melts in.

name: Oat Chocolate Chip Cookie Cups
steps: Preheat oven to 180°C / 350°F. Grease a 12-cup mini muffin tray.
Mix almond butter, honey, egg and vanilla.
Stir in oats, baking soda, salt and chocolate chips.
Press mixture into tray cups.
Bake 12-14 minutes until just set. Cool before removing.
benefits: Oat beta-glucan supports cholesterol and blood sugar regulation
Baked in cups — perfectly portioned and easy to serve
No refined flour or sugar
tip: Press a few extra chocolate chips on top after baking for a picture-perfect look.

name: Honeydew Mint Granita
steps: Blend melon, lime, mint and honey until smooth.
Pour into a flat freezer dish.
Freeze 1h then scrape with a fork every 30 minutes for 2-3 hours.
Serve in chilled glasses with a sprig of mint.
benefits: Only 50 kcal — one of the lightest possible desserts
Honeydew is high in vitamin C and potassium
Refreshing and cooling — perfect for summer
tip: Add a tiny pinch of cayenne for a surprising melon-chilli-lime granita.

name: Tahini Chocolate Cups
steps: Line a 10-hole mini muffin tray with paper cases.
Spoon a small amount of chocolate into each case. Freeze 5 minutes.
Mix tahini, honey and vanilla. Spoon over chocolate.
Top with remaining chocolate, sesame seeds and sea salt.
Freeze 20 minutes until set.
benefits: Tahini is one of the best plant sources of calcium
Sesame contains sesamin and sesamolin for liver health
Inspired by halva — Middle Eastern flavours in a healthy cup
tip: Use runny tahini (not thick paste) for the smoothest filling.

name: Blueberry Oat Squares
steps: Preheat oven to 180°C / 350°F. Line a 20x20cm tin.
Mix oats, almond flour, coconut oil and half the honey. Reserve ⅓ for topping.
Press ⅔ of oat mix into tin base.
Toss blueberries with remaining honey, lemon and cinnamon. Spread over base.
Scatter reserved oat mix over blueberries.
Bake 28-32 minutes until golden. Cool fully before cutting.
benefits: Blueberries provide pterostilbene for brain and memory health
Oat beta-glucan supports gut bacteria and cholesterol
Portable and great for meal prep
tip: Refrigerate before cutting for perfectly clean square edges.

name: Chamomile Honey Panna Cotta
steps: Dissolve gelatin in 3 tbsp cold water. Leave 5 minutes to bloom.
Heat coconut milk until steaming. Steep chamomile bags 5 minutes. Remove.
Stir in honey, vanilla and gelatin until fully dissolved.
Pour into glasses or moulds. Refrigerate 4+ hours.
Serve with a drizzle of honey and dried chamomile flowers.
benefits: Chamomile is a natural relaxant that promotes sleep and reduces anxiety
Elegant and therapeutic — particularly beneficial as an evening dessert
Dairy-free with rich coconut creaminess
tip: Don't let the coconut milk boil — steeping the chamomile in just-hot milk extracts the best flavour.

name: Apple Cinnamon Oat Bars
steps: Preheat oven to 180°C / 350°F. Line a 20x30cm tin.
Squeeze excess moisture from grated apple.
Mix all ingredients together until combined.
Press firmly into the tin.
Bake 25-30 minutes until golden. Cool completely before cutting into 12 bars.
benefits: Apple pectin is one of nature's best prebiotic fibres
Warming cinnamon helps regulate blood sugar after eating
Portable, keep well for 4 days
tip: Add a handful of raisins or dried cranberries for extra sweetness and texture.

name: Raspberry Rose Chia Parfait
steps: Mix chia seeds, almond milk, honey and rose water. Stir well.
Refrigerate at least 2h until thick and pudding-like.
Layer chia pudding, coconut yogurt and raspberries in glasses.
Top with chopped pistachios.
Serve chilled.
benefits: 9g fibre per serving — exceptional for digestive health
Rose water adds an elegant floral note with digestive benefits
Pistachios provide prebiotic fibre and complete protein
tip: Prepare the chia layer the night before for the creamiest, most set texture.
